final_answer.key_evidence_summary: All 12 alerts share one window (2026-01-17 20:09:14~20:11:09): every boutique service shows a uniform traffic/throughput drop (-65% to -72%), with latency explosion on frontend (p50 16.05ms -> 11557.08ms, +71921%), checkoutservice (17.60ms -> 7004.69ms) and cartservice (2.45ms -> 1236.06ms). Placement map from pods -o wide localizes it: worker-02 hosts cartservice, currencyservice, emailservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, shippingservice, while the loudest latency rows (frontend, checkoutservice) sit on worker-01 and only aggregate calls into those worker-02 pods (checkoutservice calls currency+shipping+email+cart, all on worker-02; frontend fans out to currency/cart/productcatalog/recommendation, all on worker-02), giving the 1.2s -> 7.0s -> 11.5s gradient; pods NOT on worker-02 and not their callers (adservice, paymentservice, redis-cart) show only the secondary throughput drop. The only node-scope anomaly in the snapshot is on worker-02: 'NETWORK_QUALITY_DEGRADED [TCP Retransmission] | Normal=0.00retrans -> Current=0.92retrans (New Spike)' - sub-1 retrans/s is noise-sized, i.e. a delay regime rather than an order-of-magnitude packet-loss regime. Node surface is healthy: worker-02 Ready=True (KubeletReady), NetworkUnavailable=False (FlannelIsUp), no Memory/Disk/PID pressure, Taints none, Unschedulable false, 8 CPU / 15.6GiB allocatable with only 20% CPU and 12% memory allocated, identical to peers in GetClusterConfiguration - ruling out scheduling, capacity, cordon, taint, kubelet/containerd and serviceaccount faults. Fault is a quality-of-path issue, not addressing: CheckServiceConnectivity succeeded on currencyservice:7000 and adservice:9555, GetErrorLogs returned nothing for frontend and cartservice, and cartservice's own log stream is dense and steady (a request every ~50-100ms, no errors) while its callers measure 1.2s - the app processes fine and the time is spent on the wire out of worker-02. Namespace events contain only Normal startup/pull rows plus transient startup istio probe timeouts on worker-01 pods - no FailedScheduling/FailedCreate/FailedMount/OOMKilled/restart mechanism.

A wave of latency and traffic drops across several services at once is usually a node-scope network story: localize by placement, not by the loudest row.

1. **Open wide, then place.** Read the pods listing in its wide form — the NODE column is the map — together with the alerts (and the error-log trail for service names, if cheap). The degrading services' pods landing on one node names the case: that node's network. If the affected services are callers of one downstream pod, that downstream pod's own usage/limits is the source — node placement alone does not make it a node story.
2. **Read the nodes listing in wide form, then let the retransmission rows decide.** Read every node's retransmission value first; do not anchor on one node before the comparison.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cartservice
  namespace: boutique
  labels:
    app: cartservice
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cartservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cartservice
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cartservice
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 5
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
      containers:
      - name: server
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop:
              - ALL
          privileged: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        image: us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/google-samples/microservices-demo/cartservice:v0.10.3
        ports:
        - containerPort: 7070
        env:
        - name: REDIS_ADDR
          value: "redis-cart:6379"
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 64Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 128Mi
